text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam and China are in a unique position to offer each other valuable exchanges of experience because both states are led by a communist party and are persisting with socialist construction, Party Secretary General Do Muoi told Qiao Shi, a senior member of China's Politburo.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has warned of possible chaos during the division of public assets in Vietnam's newly created provinces.
-- South Korea's Hyundai Group officials broke ground in the central province of Khanh Hoa for the construction of what is expected to be the biggest shipyard in Southeast Asia.
-- South Korean President Kim Young-sam arrives in Vietnam on Wednesday for a three-day official visit.
-- Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Nguyen Dy Nien told a news conference on Tuesday that natural disasters have caused damage of $628 million so far this year.

-- Visiting Chairman of the Executive Board of the Mekong Law Centre, Anand Panijarachun, told Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet on Tuesday that the centre would soon set up a representative office in Hanoi to strengthen cooperation between Vietnam and other members of the centre.

-- The Standing Committee of the National Assembly has urged governmental offices, National Assembly commissions and supreme court and inspectorate to implement resolutions, including stepping up the fight against corruption, which were worked out by the session last month.
